layout_structure.title_text: DICE: End-to-end Deformation Capture of Hand-Face Interactions from a Single Image
layout_structure.layout_description: The slide follows a centered title slide layout on a plain white background. The main title is positioned in the upper-middle section, rendered in a large, bold, black sans-serif font across three lines. Directly below the title is a centered block of text listing the fourteen contributing authors in a smaller, standard font. In the top-right corner, the ICLR conference logo is visible, accompanied by the event dates 'Apr 24 – 28, 2025'. The bottom of the slide is occupied by a horizontal row of six institutional logos representing the authors' affiliations, including Penn, the University of Hong Kong, UIUC, Max Planck Institut Informatik, the University of Cambridge, and Texas A&M University. The text density is light, with a clear focus on the title and the collaborative team.

The slide features a clean, white background with a large, bold title 'Introduction and Motivation' positioned at the top-left. In the top-right corner, there is a logo for ICLR along with the conference dates 'Apr 24 – 28, 2025'. The central content is a 2x3 grid of six rectangular images, which appear to be stills from popular memes or GIFs. These images all depict individuals touching their faces or heads in various expressions of stress, thought, or frustration. One image in the top row contains the yellow text overlay 'YOU STOP TOUCHING YOUR FACE!'. At the bottom-left of the slide, a small text line provides image credits to 'Tenor, Giphy, Gifer'. The slide has a very light text density, relying almost entirely on the visual grid to convey its message.

The slide uses a clean three-column grid layout on a white background. The title 'Introduction and Motivation' is placed at the top-left in a large, black, sans-serif font. In the top-right corner, the ICLR logo is visible alongside the conference dates 'Apr 24 – 28, 2025'. The main body of the slide consists of three vertical columns, each featuring two stacked images or diagrams with a descriptive label centered at the bottom. The left column, labeled 'Virtual Reality', contains two photographs of people wearing VR headsets. The middle column, labeled 'Character Animation', shows two 3D-style animated character busts. The right column, labeled 'Human Behavior Analysis', features a photo of a child playing with blocks above a technical diagram showing human spatial positioning and interaction vectors. A small credit line is positioned at the very bottom-left of the slide. The overall text density is light, relying heavily on visual examples to convey the application domains.

The slide features a large, bold title 'Introduction and Motivation' positioned at the top-left. In the top-right corner, there is a logo for ICLR along with the conference dates 'Apr 24 – 28, 2025'. The main body of the slide consists of a large grid of images organized into three rows, labeled (a), (b), and (c) on the left margin. The grid is split into two identical side-by-side blocks. Each block contains three columns with the headers 'Input Image', 'Front View', and 'Side View'. The 'Input Image' columns show photographs of different individuals with their hands touching or near their faces. The 'Front View' and 'Side View' columns display corresponding 3D mesh reconstructions of the head and hand from different perspectives. The layout is clean with a white background and light text density, primarily using visual examples to motivate the research problem.

The slide features a large, bold title 'Related Works' positioned at the top-left. In the top-right corner, the ICLR logo is displayed along with the conference dates 'Apr 24 – 28, 2025'. The main body of the slide is divided into two columns under bold subheadings. The left column, titled 'Hand or Face-only methods', contains two rows of figures: the top row shows facial mesh fitting and error maps (Li et al., 2017), and the bottom row shows hand pose estimation from images (Zhou et al., 2020). The right column, titled 'Whole-body methods', also contains two rows: the top row displays 3D body mesh fitting on human figures (Müller et al., 2021), and the bottom row shows a sign language speaker next to a 3D body model with a simple encoder-decoder diagram between them (Lin et al., 2023). Each figure group is followed by its respective citation in a centered text block. The background is plain white with a thin grey horizontal line at the bottom.

The slide is organized into a three-column structure under a large, bold title 'Related Works' positioned at the top-left. In the top-right corner, there is an ICLR logo with the dates 'Apr 24 – 28, 2025'. Each column has its own bold sub-heading. The left column, 'Hand or Face-only methods', contains two sets of figures: one showing face reconstruction (Li et al., 2017) and another showing hand mesh overlays (Zhou et al., 2020). The middle column, 'Whole-body methods', features two sets of figures: one depicting full-body mesh fitting (Müller et al., 2021) and another showing a person signing next to a mesh model (Lin et al., 2023). The right column, 'Optimization-based method for hand-face interaction', presents a grid of images showing real-world hand-face contact paired with 3D reconstructions from multiple views (Shimada et al., 2023). The layout is visually driven, using images to represent different research papers, with citations placed directly below each corresponding figure set. The background is plain white, and the text density is moderate.

The slide uses a clean, white background with a large, bold title 'Comparison' positioned at the top-left, followed by a smaller subtitle 'on studio-recorded images'. In the top-right corner, there is a logo for the ICLR conference featuring a pixelated head icon and the dates 'Apr 24 – 28, 2025'. The main body of the slide consists of a 2x5 grid of images for qualitative comparison. The grid is organized into five columns with headers: 'Input Image', 'Ours', 'Decaf', 'PIXIE', and 'METRO'. The 'Input Image' column contains two rows of photographs showing individuals in a studio with a green screen background, performing a hand-to-face gesture with an open mouth. The subsequent four columns display 3D mesh reconstructions corresponding to each input image, allowing for a direct visual comparison of how different methods handle facial expressions and hand-face interactions. The text density is light, prioritizing visual evidence over descriptive text.

The slide uses a clean, white-background comparison layout. At the top-left, there is a large bold title 'Comparison' with a subtitle 'on studio-recorded images' directly underneath. The top-right corner features the ICLR logo and the dates 'Apr 24 – 28, 2025'. The central content is a 2x5 grid of images. The columns are labeled 'Input Image', 'Ours', 'Decaf', 'PIXIE', and 'METRO'. The first column displays two original studio-recorded photographs of individuals against a green screen. The remaining four columns show 3D mesh reconstructions of the faces and hands from those photos, representing different computational methods. In the final column labeled 'METRO', red rectangular boxes are used to highlight specific areas of the hand reconstruction, likely indicating errors or points of comparison. The text density is light, with the focus entirely on the visual qualitative comparison between the proposed method ('Ours') and existing baselines.

The slide features a clean, white background with a comparison grid layout. The subsequent four columns display 3D mesh reconstructions of the head and hand for each input image, allowing for a qualitative comparison between the proposed method ('Ours') and three baseline methods. The text density is light, focusing primarily on visual qualitative results.

layout_structure.layout_description: The slide follows a clean, professional layout with a white background. The title is positioned at the top-left, featuring 'Comparison' in a large, bold black font and 'inference speed' in a smaller, regular black font directly underneath. In the top-right corner, the ICLR logo is visible along with the conference dates 'Apr 24 – 28, 2025'. The main body of the slide is occupied by a large, horizontally centered table. This table has a dark teal header row with white text and four data rows with alternating light gray and white backgrounds. The table columns are 'Method', 'Runtime (per image; seconds)', and 'Frames per second'. The bottom row, representing the proposed method ('Ours'), is emphasized with bold text. A small, single-line footnote at the bottom-left provides technical context: 'Runtimes are measured on a single A6000 GPU.' The slide has a light text density, focusing primarily on the quantitative comparison presented in the table.

The central content consists of two side-by-side figures: on the left is a real-world photograph of a person touching their face, and on the right is a corresponding 3D mesh reconstruction of the same head and hand pose. The text density is light, prioritizing visual demonstration over textual explanation.
